maria: Quick sync — our playback runs are diverging from prod in ways that look like kernel selection + KV cache warmup. Replay harness shows ~6% higher p95 latency vs prod for same request set. Anyone seen this pattern? :thinking:
dinesh: yup saw similar last week. Usually root cause is session boundary handling or different prefix lengths so KV hit-rate drops during replay.
kai: can you paste the exact commands/config you used to run the harness?
maria: running: ```replay-run --trace s3://traces/2026-11-02.gz --target cluster:staging --qps 200 --seed 42 --anon-mode deterministic``` and a small config: ```{"preserve_sessions":false, "interarrival_scale":1.0}```
rachel: ah — preserve_sessions:false will scramble the cache locality. For KV cache parity you need to keep sessions intact or at least preserve session-length distribution.
maria: curious — preserving sessions increases memory usage a lot in staging. Any inexpensive middle ground?
dinesh: two options: 1) preserve sessions only for top X heavy sessions (by token count), 2) preserve prefix lengths distribution and fake session IDs deterministically. Both keep hit-profile similar without full state.
kai: also check kernel selection nondeterminism. We have a RNG that picks between fused vs normal kernel when both are within margin; if replay runs on different host config it can pick different kernels and change perf. Seed the kernel selector: ```export KERNEL_SELECTOR_SEED=42```
maria: good call. I didn't set that. Could explain small p95 shifts. Anything else to get apples-to-apples?
rachel: ensure same binary + CUDA/cuDNN versions, and fix GPU clocks. We had a case where nightly driver bumped behavior. Also disable asynchronous telemetry that adds jitter.
dinesh: on anonymization: use mapping that is deterministic and many-to-one, not hashing with salts that vary across runs. Example approach: map real user ids -> pseudouser0001... in order of first-seen. That preserves per-user session lengths.
maria: we currently use salted SHA256 with a run-specific salt. I'll switch.
perf-bot: perf-checker: new run queued with seed=42, preserve_sessions=top1000, kernel_seed=42. Will post results.
kai: measurement guidance: collect per-request token timings, KV hit/miss counts, kernel name histogram, and GPU SM utilization. Compare histograms not just means. Use KS-test for distributions. If KS p<0.01 flag as divergence.
dinesh: also compute synthetic-to-prod delta on cache-hit percent by prefix-depth. If replay has lower hit-rate at shallow prefix depths that's a warmup artifact.
maria: noted. What about sampling approach? We sampled every Nth request from prod. That may bias toward longer sessions since longer sessions have more events.
rachel: prefer Poisson sampling of sessions (sample sessions uniformly, then replay full session). That preserves session-level correlations and avoids length bias.
kai: small practical check: run a tiny short-run with `--preserve-sessions=true --anon-mode=deterministic --kernel-seed=42 --qps=20` and compare kernel histogram: ```
kernel_histogram:{"fused_attention":5123,"matmul_optimized":480}
``` If the histograms differ >5% for any kernel, investigate selector thresholds.
maria: perf-bot posted results: p95 delta down to 1.2% after session-preserve + kernel_seed. KV hit-rate improved from 61% -> 78%. Still seeing odd 0.6% tail.
dinesh: check batcher heuristics — replay interarrival distribution might force suboptimal batching. If replay is bursty vs prod smooth, batcher will pick smaller accum windows. Preserve interarrival scaling by using measured interarrival CDF and sampling from it.
kai: also enable `--replay-preserve-clock` to match original timestamps if you want exact batching patterns. That requires replay infra to pace requests precisely.
maria: ok will try `--preserve-clock` and run full 30m. Any guardrails to avoid contaminating staging?
rachel: run with dedicated staging pool and fixed capacity, no autoscale. Also pin model version. If you need traffic volume emulate at lower scale but keep relative qps, just scale down uniformly.
dinesh: final step for parity assertions: (1) anonymize with deterministic mapping, (2) preserve sessions or session sampling, (3) seed kernel selector, (4) preserve interarrival distribution, (5) use same binary/drivers, (6) collect histograms and run KS tests. Document thresholds (p95 delta <2%, throughput delta <3%, KV hit delta <5%).
maria: copying checklist into the replay-run README and kicking off the 30m run. Will attach logs when done. Thanks all :pray:
infra-bot: deploy:staging pool pinned to 4 GPUs for replay window 15:10-15:45 UTC - no autoscale.
